Take Malena's list of deaths that she's already identified , combine them and make them into a common formatted list. Keep only the columns we care about for the purpose of death coding


```{r}
#| label: setup


pacman::p_load("here", "tidyverse", "googlesheets4", "lubridate", "janitor")

here::i_am("death-certificates/02-icf-deaths.qmd")

```


Malena had found about 480 deaths in RHA, non-RHA and government addresses. These are in different sheets with slightly different layouts. Standardize them as I read them in. 

```{r}
#| label: get-all-malena-sheets

icf_deaths_googlesheet <- "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gOmJrS_-U9knRArSrUeC5SwQ8Mf-WkY9oabl3OuBxu8/"



rha_deaths <- read_sheet(icf_deaths_googlesheet, sheet="RHA Deaths")  |> 
  select ( death_id , `Facility Name`) |>  mutate (`Facility Owner` = "RHA") 

oth_deaths <- read_sheet (icf_deaths_googlesheet, sheet="Non-RHA, Non-Gov") |> 
  select ( death_id, `Facility Name`,  `Facility Owner`) 

gov_deaths <- read_sheet ( icf_deaths_googlesheet, sheet = "Gov")  |> 
  select ( death_id ) |> 
  mutate ( `Facility Name` = NA_character_, 
           `Facility Owner` = "NC Government")

```

Now combine into a single list, retaining the name of the source sheet. (By hand)


```{r}
#| label: malena-death-list


combined_list <- 
  bind_rows ( 
    "RHA Deaths" = rha_deaths,
    "Non-RHA, Non-Gov" = oth_deaths,
    "Gov" = gov_deaths, 
    .id = "df_source"
  )

# get a list of unique death_id values for the SQL statement
where_list <- combined_list |> distinct ( death_id) |> pull()

```

(this list is the same number of rows as the spreadsheet so there are no duplicates)

Connect to the death database and extract just those death IDs from our larger 2020-forward death certificates data.

```{r}
#| label: connect-to-certs

library(duckdb)
con <- duckdb::dbConnect( duckdb(), here("death-certificates/data/deaths2020up.duckdb"))
# dbListTables(con)

```




```{r}
#| label: extract-matching-certs

all_deaths <- dbGetQuery( con, 
      glue::glue_sql ("SELECT * FROM deaths_from2020 WHERE death_id IN ({where_list*}) ",
                  .con = con)
) |> 
  select ( death_id, dod, dob, manner, lname, gname, stnum_r:zip9_r, 
           dplace, dinsti, address_d:zip9_d, countytext_d, man_uc:autop ,  howinj)  


```

(make sure to disconnect from the database and shut it down)

```{r}
#| label: disconnect-certs

dbDisconnect(con, shutdown=TRUE)
rm ( con)

```

Now I can link them back to where it happened


```{r}
#| label: join-to-certs

deaths_working <-  
  combined_list |> 
  inner_join ( all_deaths , join_by ( death_id) )


```

save this for later


```{r}
#| label: save-icf-list

saveRDS(deaths_working, here("death-certificates/processed/02-icf-deaths.RDS"))


```
